newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa down on origin selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa down on origin selling.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures fell on origin selling, combined with a lack of industry buyers, traders said.
The most active month, March, last traded down seven sterling at 887 sterling, just off a low of 885 stg. March volume was 2,227 lots of a total 4,451
"There's nothing bullish around," was one trader's explanation of the fundamental reason for the fall.
There is origin selling, he explained, but long holders then discover they can't find any buyers to hedge it off against.

Another explained that London cocoa futures had managed to get off lows as a reaction to a better than expected New York performance. New York cocoa slumped at its opening, but did not get as far as the $10-$15/tonne due.

Traders had hoped that cocoa could break through resistance above 900 stg on March, which was created by origin sellers above that point. But instead, the origin selling has come down to meet a lower market, while the industry has held back.
One result was some disappointed long liquidation, another trader said.

In the physical market, Ghana cocoa purchases in the 13th week of the 1996/97 season ending January 9 were 16,364 tonnes compared with 8,950 tonnes in the week ending January 11, 1996, the Ghana Cocoa Board said on Wednesday.

A delegation of cocoa industry representatives and lending officials will head for Ivory Coast next week to monitor progress on the country's privatisation programme, Dutch Cocoa Association director Louis Bensdorp said.
